questions.stem: Fact 8 asks how to locate a key on the circle of fifths.

answer.exemplar: Start at C major and move clockwise one fifth for each added sharp, or counterclockwise one fifth for each added flat; the key's position follows its sharp or flat count.

questions.explanation: Each clockwise fifth adds a sharp and each counterclockwise fifth adds a flat.

questions.explanation: Clockwise from C major, six fifth steps reach F sharp major, so the distance is six fifths. Counting five stops one fifth short.
questions.hint: Count the steps on the circle.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Finding the number of an interval
questions.learningObjective: Explain finding the number of an interval
questions.stem: Fact 52 asks why interval number ignores quality.

answer.exemplar: Interval number counts letter names inclusively, while quality describes size in semitones; thus a major third and minor third both have number three.

questions.explanation: Number counts letter names and quality counts semitones, so they are independent.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Whole steps in the major scale pattern
questions.learningObjective: Count whole steps in the major scale pattern
questions.stem: Fact 53 checks the major scale pattern; how many whole steps appear between the first and last note?

options.text: Five whole steps, the correct count
Six whole steps, adding an extra
Seven whole steps, confusing with seven notes
options.misconception: confuses seven notes with seven whole steps

questions.explanation: The major scale pattern W W H W W W H has seven steps, and five of them are whole steps while two are half steps. Counting four stops one short, and counting six or seven confuses whole steps with total steps.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Tracing a semitone chain through a melody
questions.learningObjective: Trace a semitone chain through a melody
questions.stem: Fact 54 plots a melody; what is the semitone total from C to E flat to G?
questions.explanation: C to E flat is three semitones and E flat to G is four more, giving seven total.
questions.hint: Add the steps between consecutive notes.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Octave equivalence
questions.learningObjective: Identify octave-equivalent notes
questions.stem: Fact 55 counts semitones between octave-equivalent notes.
questions.explanation: Octave-equivalent notes share a pitch class and are separated by twelve semitones. Any smaller count would fall short of a full octave.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Scientific pitch notation and middle C
questions.learningObjective: Explain scientific pitch notation and middle C
questions.stem: Fact 56 asks how octave numbers change across middle C.

answer.exemplar: Octave numbers increase as pitch rises, so notes just above middle C remain in octave four until C5, which begins octave five.

questions.explanation: Octave numbers increase as pitch rises, so notes just above middle C remain in octave four until C5, which begins octave five. The number does not change at middle C itself.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Locating a key on the circle of fifths
questions.learningObjective: Locate a key on the circle of fifths
questions.stem: Fact 57 locates a key; which key has two flats?

options.misconception: counts four flats instead of two

questions.explanation: On the circle of fifths, two counterclockwise fifths from C major give B flat major with two flats. F major has one flat, E flat has three, and A flat has four.
questions.hint: Counterclockwise from C: F, B flat.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Measuring distance on the circle of fifths
questions.learningObjective: Measure distance on the circle of fifths
questions.stem: Fact 58 plots two keys; how many fifths separate D major from A major?

options.misconception: confuses adjacent keys with the same key

questions.explanation: D to A is one clockwise fifth, so the distance is one fifth. Zero treats them as the same key, and two or three counts extra steps.
questions.hint: Count the steps on the circle.

questions.topic: Finding the number of an interval
questions.learningObjective: Find the number of an interval
questions.stem: Fact 59 asks for the number of a major sixth interval.
questions.explanation: A major sixth spans six letter names, so its interval number is six. Counting five or seven would misread the inclusive letter count.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Whole steps in the major scale pattern
questions.learningObjective: Explain whole steps in the major scale pattern
questions.stem: Fact 60 asks how many whole steps appear in the major scale pattern.

answer.exemplar: The major scale pattern W W H W W W H contains five whole steps and two half steps, totaling seven steps.

questions.explanation: The major scale pattern W W H W W W H has seven steps total, and five of them are whole steps while two are half steps. Counting all seven as whole steps would ignore the two required half steps.
